title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the Douro and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Dry wines are labelled Douro DOC; fortified wines Porto DOC. Port labels show the style: Ruby, Tawny, LBV, Vintage, Colheita, or an age like 20 Years Old. Quinta means estate. The IVDP, the Douro and Port institute, seals each bottle. Vinhas velhas means old vines.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Dry Douro reds suit roast kid, lamb, bacalhau with roasted potatoes, and game. Ruby and Vintage Port suit Stilton and dark chocolate. Tawny suits crème brûlée, nuts, caramel desserts and Portuguese pastries like pastéis de nata. White Port with tonic is Porto's aperitif. Serve tawny slightly cool.
steps.highlight: Stilton with Vintage; nuts with tawny

steps.explanation: Porto tónico, white Port and tonic.

steps.title: Serving Port
steps.body: Serve ruby and Vintage Port at about 16 degrees, tawnies at 10 to 14, white Port chilled. Decant Vintage Port and unfiltered LBV for sediment. Opened tawnies last weeks; Vintage Port is best within a day or two.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Douro DOC is dry; Porto DOC is fortified
Dry reds suit lamb; Vintage Port suits Stilton
Decant Vintage Port; tawnies keep after opening
